# viettelcloud_lb_server_group (Resource)

Manage a Viettel Cloud Load Balancer Server Group.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "viettelcloud_lb_server_group" "web_pool" {
  load_balancer = { id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001" }
  name          = "web-pool"
  description   = "Web servers backend pool"
  protocol      = "HTTP"
  algorithm     = "ROUND_ROBIN"

  health_check = {
    monitor_type     = "HTTP"
    delay            = 10
    timeout          = 5
    max_retries      = 3
    max_retries_down = 3
    http_method      = "GET"
    path             = "/healthz"
    expected_codes   = "200,204"
  }
}

resource "viettelcloud_lb_server_group" "app_pool" {
  load_balancer = { id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001" }
  name          = "app-pool"
  description   = "Application servers backend pool with cookie persistence"
  protocol      = "HTTP"
  algorithm     = "LEAST_CONNECTIONS"

  session_persistence = {
    type        = "APP_COOKIE"
    cookie_name = "SESSIONID"
  }

  health_check = {
    monitor_type     = "TCP"
    delay            = 15
    timeout          = 5
    max_retries      = 3
    max_retries_down = 3
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `algorithm` (String) Load balancing algorithm: ROUND_ROBIN, LEAST_CONNECTIONS, SOURCE_IP, or SOURCE_IP_PORT.
- `load_balancer` (Attributes) Load Balancer that owns this server group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--load_balancer))
- `name` (String) Name of the Server Group.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol for the server group: HTTP, HTTPS, PROXY, PROXYV2, TCP, or UDP.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description. Omission preserves the current value. Set an empty string to clear it.
- `enable_h2` (Boolean) Enable HTTP/2 support. Omission uses the backend value and preserves it on update. Set false to disable it, except for HTTPS, which always uses HTTP/2.
- `health_check` (Attributes) Health check monitor configuration. Omit to create or update without a health check. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--health_check))
- `session_persistence` (Attributes) Session persistence configuration. Creation without this object requests NONE. Removal preserves the current value. Set type to NONE to disable persistence. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--session_persistence))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the Server Group was created (RFC3339).
- `id` (String) Server Group ID (UUID).
- `member_count` (Number) Number of backend members in the Server Group.
- `provisioning_status` (String) Provisioning status of the Server Group.
- `status` (String) Operational status of the Server Group.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the Server Group was last updated (RFC3339).

<a id="nestedatt--load_balancer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `load_balancer`

Required:

- `id` (String) Load Balancer ID (UUID).


<a id="nestedatt--health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `health_check`

Required:

- `delay` (Number) Delay between health checks in seconds.
- `max_retries` (Number) Number of successful checks before considering server online.
- `max_retries_down` (Number) Number of failed checks before considering server offline.
- `monitor_type` (String) Monitor type: HTTP, HTTPS, PING, SCTP, TCP, TLS-HELLO, or UDP-CONNECT.
- `timeout` (Number) Health check timeout in seconds.

Optional:

- `expected_codes` (String) Expected HTTP status codes, e.g. 200 or 200-299 (required for HTTP/HTTPS).
- `http_method` (String) HTTP method to use (required for HTTP/HTTPS): GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, TRACE, CONNECT.
- `path` (String) HTTP URL path to check (required for HTTP/HTTPS).


<a id="nestedatt--session_persistence"></a>
### Nested Schema for `session_persistence`

Optional:

- `cookie_name` (String) Cookie name when session persistence type is APP_COOKIE. Omit it for other types.
- `type` (String) Session persistence type: NONE, HTTP_COOKIE, APP_COOKIE, or SOURCE_IP. Required when session_persistence is configured.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a Load Balancer Server Group using composite ID <load_balancer_id>/<server_group_id>.
terraform import viettelcloud_lb_server_group.web_pool 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002
```
